title: Perf incident postmortem: SLO miss and customer escalation (hotfix validation)
content:
Summary:

On 2026-03-21 we observed a sustained SLO miss for the hosted text-generation endpoint (route: /v1/generate, model: rdx-13b-v1). The customer-facing p95 latency target is 250ms; observed p95 peaked at ~420ms and p99 at ~1.8s for a 3-hour window starting ~01:10 UTC. A high-severity customer escalation was opened at 01:45 UTC.

Impact:
- Affected customers: ~15 high-traffic customers on the hosted cluster (shared pool).
- User-visible: increased tail latency and timeouts for chat sessions with long histories (>1k tokens).
- Billing/throughput: throughput dropped ~18% during the incident due to request queuing and autoscaler oscillation.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-21 00:55: Alerting: rate of p95>250ms started increasing (oncall noticed).
- 2026-03-21 01:10: p95 consistently >350ms. Pager duty triggered.
- 2026-03-21 01:20: Customer Success notified; customer escalation opened at 01:45.
- 2026-03-21 01:35: Eng SRE and serving-runtime oncall joined war room.
- 2026-03-21 02:05: Initial mitigation: increased cluster capacity (spin-up additional nodes) and enforced conservative batching limits.
- 2026-03-21 02:25: Root-cause hypothesis formed based on profiling (see below).
- 2026-03-21 03:10: Hotfix deployed to canary: revert of kernel-routing change + adjust KV cache eviction threshold.
- 2026-03-21 03:45: Canary metrics showed p95 back to ~240ms; gradual roll-out.
- 2026-03-21 04:30: Full roll-out complete. Customer notified; monitoring continued for 24h.

What we profiled / observed:
- KV cache hit rate dropped from baseline ~92% to ~56% during the incident window for long-chat workloads. This correlated strongly with increased end-to-end latency.
- GPU metrics: tail GPU SM utilization spiking to 95% with frequent stalls; overall host CPU context switching/IO wait increased (dstat/iostat showed elevated io wait).
- Serving runtime traces (pprof/flamegraphs): increased time in the "batch assembly" and "kv-cache-miss path" code paths. The dispatch layer selected an alternative attention kernel (kernel-b) for many requests due to recent kernel-routing heuristics; kernel-b has worse memory locality for long sequences and higher per-token latency when KV cache misses are high.
- Autoscaler behavior: scale-up was triggered but nodes entered an overloaded state because each request cost much more GPU time (due to cache misses + kernel inefficiency). This caused request queuing and increased tail latency, which in turn triggered further scaling and destabilized scheduling.
- Workload pattern: long-history chat sessions with frequent incremental updates (many small requests that reuse KV cache heavily) experienced the worst degradation.

Root cause (short):
A recent optimization change to the kernel-routing heuristics increased the likelihood of selecting kernel-b for sequence lengths and runtime signals common to long-chat workloads. Kernel-b performs worse under high KV cache-miss rates because of suboptimal memory access patterns. Simultaneously, a conservative KV cache eviction tuning change (rolled last week) lowered the effective cache footprint for multi-session pods, reducing hit rate. The combination created a cascade: reduced KV hit rate -> more expensive per-request compute paths -> overloaded GPUs -> autoscaler oscillation -> higher queuing/tail latency -> SLO miss.

Contributing factors:
- The kernel-routing change lacked a workload-oriented canary across long-history chat patterns. Perf testing focused on short-burst synthetic loads and missed the long-history tail case.
- KV cache eviction tuning was conservative and not validated against multi-tenant long-session workloads.
- Observability gap: KV cache hit-rate was not part of our primary SLO dashboards, so the signal arrived late in the incident.
- Autoscaler thresholds were tuned for throughput-driven spikes, not persistent per-request cost increases.

Mitigation & hotfix validation summary:
- Immediate mitigation: increased cluster capacity and conservative batching limits to reduce queuing while we investigated. This bought ~60 minutes of breathing room.
- Hotfix 1 (canary): revert kernel-routing heuristic to previous stable rule-set (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1428). Also adjusted KV cache eviction threshold from 0.20 -> 0.35 effective per-pod footprint.
- Canary validation steps:
  - Synthetic replay: replayed captured traffic from 2026-03-20 long-chat traces against the canary nodes. Measured KV hit-rate, p95/p99 latency, and GPU SM utilization.
  - A/B test: routed 10% of traffic from affected tenant group to canary for 30 minutes and compared metrics.
  - Profiling: pprof/flamegraph before and after showed batch assembly time reduced by ~48% for long-history sessions; KV hit-rate recovered to ~88% on canary.
- Rollout: after 30 minutes of stable canary metrics, rolled to remaining pool over 40 minutes. Monitored aggressively for regressions.

Validation numbers (canary vs incident):
- p95 latency: incident 420ms -> canary 240ms -> baseline 220ms.
- p99 latency: incident 1800ms -> canary 520ms -> baseline 480ms.
- KV cache hit-rate: incident 56% -> canary 88% -> baseline 92%.
- GPU SM utilization (tail): incident 95% -> canary 62% -> baseline 60%.

Customer communication:
- Customer Success and Support issued interim status updates during the incident window and final post-incident update once rollout completed. The main escalated customer received a technical summary and follow-up offer for a dedicated tuning session.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Rollback safety net: add automatic rollback if p95 increases >15% vs baseline during large rollouts (owner: Marcus Li, due 2026-04-05).
- Add KV cache hit-rate to primary SLO dashboard and alerting (owner: Rohit Patel, due 2026-03-31).
- Add long-history chat synthetic load tests to CI perf suite (owner: Lena Gomez, due 2026-04-07).
- Autoscaler tuning: add hysteresis for per-request-cost-driven scaling and a "persistent cost" detection (owner: Priya Kapoor, due 2026-04-10).
- Post-deployment regression test: integrate kernel-routing A/B smoke tests in canary pipeline (owner: Ava Chen, due 2026-04-01).

Longer-term follow-ups:
- Revisit kernel-routing decision logic with a cost-model that incorporates KV hit-rate and sequence-length distribution; design an offline evaluator to predict per-kernel cost for representative workloads.
- Explore per-tenant cache-sizing or session pinning to isolate long-history heavy tenants.
- Document best-practice perf-validation checklist for changes that affect kernel selection, caching, or batching.

Notes / debugging artifacts (short):
- pprof traces: saved under perf-traces/2026-03-21/ (refer to linked_artifacts in ticket).
- Capture for replay: s3://redwood-perf/replays/2026-03-21-long-chat-01.trace
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1428

Lessons learned (post-incident):
- Optimizations need workload diversity in canaries: our canary strategy missed long-history chat patterns.
- Important internal signals (KV cache hit-rate, per-request GPU-time) should be surfaced to SLO dashboards.
- Small tuning changes to memory/caching can magnify when combined with kernel selection differences. Test interactions.

Appendix: quick debugging checklist used during incident (for oncall playbook):
1) Check p95/p99 and per-route traffic breakdown.
2) Check KV cache hit-rate and per-session cache occupancy.
3) Inspect kernel-routing histograms and recent deploys to routing heuristics.
4) Profile GPU SM utilization and NVTX traces for stalls.
5) If necessary, revert kernel-routing or adjust cache thresholds in canary before cluster-wide rollout.

Document history:
- Created by Ava Chen 2026-03-22 initial draft.
- Added profiling results and canary validation 2026-03-23 (Rohit).
- Customer communication summary added 2026-03-24 (CS).
- Final validation numbers and action items updated 2026-03-28 (Ava).

Triage note: This doc is intended as the working postmortem for the serving-runtime team and CS escalation. Please add comments inline or via the linked Jira ticket INF-867.
